content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question about configuring network inputs in [product_name] programming when using fixed addresses such as NI NO, etc. Should I use these constant addresses directly in the program, for example, set NI4 to address V1246.3? If so, why does the [product_name] software set that address as the default in the block? Also, when creating a tag list in the engineering platform, should I use the memory mapping addresses (like VM) or are Q0.1 and V1064.1 treated equivalently? Since I'm new to this, it would be great to find all relevant info in one place. This topic is closely related to my previous post split from “[document]”.
Welcome to the forum, [user_name]. There are multiple approaches to configuration, and it's really up to personal preference; there isn't a universal best method.

I understand there are different ways to set this up. It seems I can't assign network input addresses higher than 850, so I have to also set a custom address. Regarding tag assignment in the engineering platform—are I and Q addresses directly mapped to these fixed addresses? It's difficult to test since I can't simulate both the controller and the interface at once, especially because the controller is physically at the site.
You can simulate the interface using the engineering platform, and with a real [product_name], establish a connection.
The engineering platform provides a driver for [product_name]. For Q and I tags, you can simply use Q0.0 and I0.0. Instruction blocks may require using the VM mapped address when creating tags.
Whether you use Q1 or V1064.0, the outcome remains the same.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers on configuring variable memory addresses and I/Q tag mapping in [product_name] programs, particularly when using the engineering platform and constant address assignments. There's uncertainty over when to apply VM mapped addresses versus standard I/Q notation for tag setup and block programming. Users experience limitations with address ranges and simulation, which affects clarity for those new to the topic and impacts implementation efficiency.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want clear instructions about whether to use constant VM addresses or I/Q format in both [product_name] programming and engineering platform tag creation, including how they correspond. They also seek easy-to-use simulation options suitable for remote work environments.
